maria: Quick check-in: I want to nail down the admission state machine we discussed last week. The main open questions are eviction ordering (kv-cache vs batch-evict), where preemptive-drain lives, and how fallbacks are signaled. Sketch below.

jake: sketch please! this has been causing weird node-level spikes in prod.

maria: ASCII sketch of the state transitions: 
``
[request arrival] -> route-eval -> kv-probe
  kv-hit -> short-circuit -> respond
  kv-miss -> admission-state = PENDING
PENDING -> admit-check (soft-reserve, tenant_quota)
  admit ok -> ENQUEUED -> lane BATCHER or MICROLANE
  admit deny -> FALLBACK or REJECT depending on policy
ENQUEUED -> WAIT (batch_delay) -> READY -> allocate-slot -> RUN
RUN -> emit telemetry -> COMPLETE

Signals: kv-evict, preemptive-drain, node-pressure, manual-evict
Order invariant we want: kv-evict should make in-flight PENDING requests re-evaluate before enqueue.
``

olivia: Two concrete proposals for eviction ordering: (A) synchronous re-eval: kv-evict posts recheck events to admission and those PENDING requests re-run kv-probe before enqueue. Pros: correctness. Cons: extra latency and thundering rechecks.

(B) eventual recheck: allow PENDING -> ENQUEUED, mark batch entries with kv-hit=false tag and perform a KV-check at batching time; if miss then fallback or re-route. Pros: avoids immediate rework. Cons: wasted batching and potential correctness holes for cached responses.

samir: My gut: do A for streaming/prefix-KV flows (where correctness matters) and B for best-effort cached-prefetch flows. We should formalize with policy bits in route-config: `cache_consistency: STRONG | EVENTUAL`.

devon: Telemetry hooks to add: `admission.recheck_count`, `evict.trigger_source`, `batch.kv_miss_at_emit` and per-lane `starvation_seconds`. Also trace spans across recheck->enqueue so we can find thundering patterns.

maria: Thanks. Another open item: preemptive-drain. I suggest it be implemented as a soft signal from executor to admission with a TTL and reason, e.g., `preemptive-drain: {reason: node_pressure, ttl_ms: 2000}`. Admission should prioritize draining long-running batches in nodes under pressure.

jake: Important: draining should not cause SLA violations for high-priority tenants. We need a priority-preserve rule: `if priority >= route_min_priority -> do not preempt`. Put this in proto.

maria: Example proto fields I plan to add: `message RoutePolicy { optional QoS qos = 1; optional Fallback fallback = 2; optional CacheConsistency cache_consistency = 3; optional PreemptPolicy preempt = 4; }` and `message PreemptPolicy { int32 ttl_ms = 1; float borrow_limit_pct = 2; repeated string protected_tenants = 3; }`.

olivia: Test matrix idea: 1) kv-evict ordering: inject evict between arrival and enqueue, assert recheck semantics for STRONG/EVENTUAL. 2) preemptive-drain correctness under node_pressure with protected_tenants. 3) borrowing stress: ensure small tenants are not starved when large tenant borrows up to borrow_limit_pct.

samir: Borrowing algorithm sketch: each tenant has (reserved_slots, used_slots). Borrow capacity = max(0, total_free * borrow_limit_pct - tenant.borrow_score). Borrow_score decays over time. Simple leaky-bucket-like decay.

devon: For canary rollout: 5% traffic initially, observe p50/p90/p99 for cache-hit paths and non-cache paths separately, plus `recheck_count` and deploybot metrics. Auto-rollback thresholds: p99 +12% or `admission.recheck_count` > 3% of requests.

maria: Ops-bot, can you snapshot node-42 queue-depth and last eviction events?

ops-bot: snapshot: node-42 queue-depth=1378 at 1747420005, last-evict-events=[{"time":1747419900, "source":"kv-ttl"}, {"time":1747419990, "source":"manual-evict"}]

jake: That manual-evict at 1747419990 might have raced with a deploy that changed route-configs. We should add a deploy-id annotation to manual-evict events.

maria: Agree. Action items: (1) I'll open RFC follow-up with proto diffs + the two eviction strategies spelled out. (2) @samir will prototype borrowing and decay. (3) @devon will add telemetry spans and the recheck metrics. (4) @olivia will draft test matrix and canary checklist.

samir: I'll try to get a basic simulator up this week to exercise borrow heuristics.

devon: I'll add `admission.recheck_count` instrumentation to the staging runtime.

maria: Thanks all. Let's reconvene after the RFC edit and simulator results.
